title: October deep re-check: does pre-market range % hold up as a real exclusion filter on live-collected data, now that there's enough depth for a proper threshold-vs-random-control test?

tables.name: Pre-market exclusion thresholds vs baseline+random-control, live data (9 tested)

notes: September's 3 live reads (r=-0.28 to -0.20, all p<0.001) were all measured as a raw correlation within the accumulation-sourced shortlist, never run through this project's full threshold-vs-random-control bar -- the same gap that produced 6 false positives in the 09-17 signal-discovery batch for OTHER signals. This closes that gap using sentiment_outcome_history.json's real simulated_pct (the live staircase-exit mechanics, not a proxy) joined against premarket_volatility_tracking.json, for a much larger resolved sample (446) than September's performance.json-windowed joins (177-215) could reach.

conclusion.verdict: DISCARD -- DOES NOT HOLD UP AT REAL DEPTH
conclusion.summary: 0 threshold(s) beat both baseline and their own random-shuffle control on both TRAIN and VAL at n=446 real resolved candidate-days -- the correlation does not survive a proper random-control test at real depth.
